title: BinaryPaper conformance vector manifest
description: Describes one conformance vector: its inputs, the operation to perform, and the exact expected outcome. Language-neutral: paths always use '/', every external file is hashed, and unknown properties are rejected so a typo fails loudly instead of silently disabling a check.

schemaVersion.description: Version of this schema. Incremented only for a breaking change to the manifest shape.

protocol.description: The capsule wire version this vector exercises.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique across the suite. Never reused for different bytes.

category.description: What this vector is for. 'positive' expects success; every other value is a family of expected rejections.

title.description: One-line human summary. Informative; never a substitute for the specification.

operation.description: What an implementation should do with the inputs. 'recover' runs the full pipeline to restored bytes; 'inspect' stops before authentication and reports public metadata only.

inputs.description: Every input file, in the order they should be presented. Ordering matters for session and duplicate cases.

password.description: Test password for an encrypted vector. Absent means no password is supplied.

kind.description: Always 'public-test-value'. These are published test data and are deliberately not examples of good passwords.

expected.description: The exact required outcome. A conforming implementation matches this or fails the vector.

result.description: 'success' or the stable failure category from the protocol specification.

stage.description: The validation stage at which a rejection occurs. Required for every failure; forbidden for success. Rejecting at the wrong stage is a conformance defect even when the input is correctly rejected.

outputs.description: For a successful recovery, the exact restored artifacts.

payloadKind.description: The restored payload kind, for a successful recovery.

displayName.description: The manifest display name, for a successful recovery.

capsule.description: Public frame/session metadata a reader must report identically.

provenance.description: How these bytes came to exist, so they can be regenerated or audited rather than trusted.

recipe.description: Deterministic steps that reproduce the inputs.

derivedFrom.description: For a negative vector, the positive vector id it was mutated from.

mutation.description: The exact mutation applied, including whether the CRC-32C was recomputed. Recomputing is required whenever the intended failure stage is after the frame-digest check.

crcRecomputed.description: Whether the frame digest was recomputed after mutation. A vector that intends to fail after stage 3 must set this true, or it silently tests the CRC check instead.

path.description: Path relative to the manifest's own directory. Always '/' separated, on every host platform.

role.description: What this file is, for readability. Informative.

encoding.description: For a text artifact, its exact byte semantics. Text fixtures are byte artifacts, not platform-native text files.
